What classical music pieces would improve just by cutting out some parts?

One song that I've come back to again and again in my study and appreciation of the classical guitar is a piece from Francisco Tarrega called "Recuerdos de la Alhambra."

The piece starts out with a slightly somber A-minor part, which repeats once. Every time I've played it, that beginning always feels like a real chore that I wish I didn't have to drag my feet through to get to the second half, which is in a much brighter A-major. As such, I used to think it would be nice to play the piece by cutting out the A-minor section entirely, but without the contrasting moods, and the build-up of the first part, the magic of the second part is lost. It certainly is still beautiful, but without the somber opening, the happier part that follows doesn't have the same rewarding charm that it otherwise would have.

As such, in recent years, I've performed the piece by playing the opening minor part only once, omitting its repeat, and proceeding onward to the happier end.

I always felt like it was a song you could play for young boy at some carnival, who's sad and worried about his future, as I was many years ago.
